01.r: Marks the time: when each period of seven years runs out.
01.n: Literally 'from the end of'. Gesenius gives the noun as end, extremity, of space or of time, and notes that with this 'from' it means at the end, after, as in 'after forty days'.

02.r: The number of years in the cycle.
02.n: The Hebrew has no 'every'; the KJV, ASV, JPS and BSB add it to make the repeating cycle plain. The DRC makes the number an ordinal, 'the seventh year'.

03.n: Gesenius suggests the word properly means a repetition, the return of the sun's course or of the seasons.

04.r: Each Israelite is to put the remission into effect.
04.n: The ordinary verb for doing and making, imperfect, used as a command. The 'you' is singular, as through this law. The BSB folds this verb and the noun after it into 'cancel debts'.

05.r: A letting go of claims: what this is, the next verse explains.
05.n: BDB: a letting drop of exactions; the brief's lexicon adds a temporary remitting, release from debt. Gesenius gives remission, release, citing this verse, and calls the year of remission the year of jubilee; in this law it falls every seventh year. Geneva says 'freedome'.

01.n: διά, here 'after an interval of', 'every': 'through seven years'.

05.n: ἄφεσις, 'release, letting go'. It is the word the New Testament uses for the forgiveness of sins.
